1) [Seif 1] It is forbidden to hold a bare Sefer Torah, etc. For so it is [stated] at the end of Megillah and in Shabbos, folio 14a: Rabbi Parnach said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: anyone who holds a bare Sefer Torah is buried bare, without that mitzvah. For the Tosafos wrote there: some explain 'the mitzvah of holding' [is lost], and it is difficult -- what is the novelty? It is obvious that he has no reward, since he did not perform the mitzvah properly. Therefore the Riva explained, 'without that mitzvah' that he performed at that time: that if he held a bare Sefer Torah and read from it, he has no reward from the reading; and likewise if he held it to roll it or to correct it. End of his language. And so the Tosafos wrote in Shabbos there; and so wrote the Rosh; and the Beis Yosef cited it. And it is implied from the words of the Gemara and the explanation of the aforementioned Riva that this [prohibition] that it is forbidden to hold a bare Sefer Torah is specifically if there is a mitzvah in that holding, such as at the time of hagbahah or the reading or the gelilah after the reading, or if he needs to correct something in it during the reading; for it says 'he is buried bare without that mitzvah.' But if he does not hold it for [the purpose of] a mitzvah, such as when the Sefer Torah is taken to place it in another place, or when he rolls it before the reading to the place of the reading, or when he holds the sheets of the Sefer Torah not at the time of the reading in order to correct them, and the like -- there is no prohibition to hold [it] without a covering, since there is no mitzvah in that holding. And so wrote the Rashash, of blessed memory, in Shaar HaKavanos, folio 49b, that this obligation is only at the time of the reading of the Sefer Torah in public, when supernal lights are revealed as stated; but not at the time of the reading, such as when one needs to repair it or for another matter, there is nothing to it. End of his language. And it is reasonable that he means specifically at the time of the reading, when there is a mitzvah and also when the lights are revealed; but if not at the time of the reading, or when there is no mitzvah in that holding, there is nothing to it, as is implied from the words of the Gemara. And see the Ben Ish Chai, parashas Toldos, ot 18, who wrote that if, at the time that he opens the Sefer Torah to show the writing to the congregation, he sees that it is not open at the parashah that they read, and he needs to roll two or three columns, he must hold [it] with a covering even according to the words of the Rashash, of blessed memory, since it is explained in Shaar HaKavanos there that at the time that he opens the Sefer Torah in the Heichal in order to read, the illumination of the Torah written within it is revealed outward to the entire congregation; and he wrote that the shaliach tzibbur must likewise take care, at the time that he reads in public and a column is completed such that he needs to draw the sheet, that he hold [it] by means of a covering; see there. However, according to what was stated, it appears that there is no proof for this from the words of the Rashash, of blessed memory; and also from the words of the Gemara and the explanation of the Riva, of blessed memory, that we brought above, it appears that there is no prohibition except specifically if there is a mitzvah in that holding, and in this matter there is no mitzvah; nevertheless one should be stringent. And see our words above in siman 134, ot 10.
2) There: It is forbidden to hold a bare Sefer Torah, etc. The Beis Yosef wrote that the Mordechai wrote that this applies to [holding with] bare hands generally, but if he took [it] and did not divert his attention, we are not particular. Until here. And the Beis Yosef wrote: and it is possible that upon this the Ashkenazim rely, who hold a bare Sefer Torah at the time that they raise it to show the writing to the people; however, I found written in the name of the Agudah that even close to the taking it is said [to be forbidden]. End of his language. However, the Rama, of blessed memory, in the Darkei Moshe, ot 2, wrote: I am of their descendants and I have not seen this custom among them; rather, on the contrary, they are careful not to touch a bare Sefer Torah; but with other holy writings they are not careful at all, and I have never seen anyone who was concerned about this with other sefarim. End of his language. And the Bach wrote on this 'it is forbidden to hold [it] bare,' etc.: the explanation is that the reader from the Torah must hold the pillars of the Torah at the time of the blessing and reading, as [stated] above at the end of siman 139, and it is forbidden for him to hold the pillars of the scroll without a covering; and our custom that they are not careful in this relies on what the Mordechai wrote in the name of the Ra'avyah at the end of Megillah, that this applies to [holding with] bare hands generally, but if he took [it] and did not divert his attention we are not particular, etc.; and he concluded that every G-d-fearing person should not hold the pillars of a bare Sefer Torah without a covering. And likewise I have seen among the meticulous that both at the time that they read and at the time that they raise [it], they hold the pillars of the Sefer Torah by means of the corner of the tallis; and I have heard that so they practice in the land of Ashkenaz, and it is proper. End of his language. And so is the view of the Magen Avraham at the beginning of the siman, that even the pillars it is forbidden to hold bare; see there. And the Pri Chadash wrote, ot 1, that from the words of the Bach it appears that even [when the scroll is] wrapped in a covering it is forbidden for him to hold the pillars of the scroll without a covering or by means of the corner of the tallis; and this is not [so], for although when it is bare it is forbidden to hold its pillars, as the Mahari"t, part 1, siman 136, inferred from the words of the Rambam, and so it appears from the words of the Beis Yosef -- but when it is wrapped in a covering, it is obvious that it is permitted to hold the pillars of the scroll even without a covering. End of his language. And so wrote the Yad Aharon in the Hagahos Beis Yosef. However, the Nehar Shalom, ot 1, wrote that if the Sefer Torah is wrapped in a covering, according to all opinions it is permitted to hold the pillars without a covering; and that which the Beis Yosef wrote, that the Ashkenazim hold a bare Sefer Torah at the time that they raise [it], etc., means that they would hold it without a covering around it; see there. And so wrote the Maamar Mordechai, ot 1, that if the Sefer Torah is wrapped in a covering it is permitted to hold the pillars without a covering; see there. And so wrote the Mishbetzos Zahav, ot 1, and the Eshel Avraham at the beginning of the siman; see there. And see the responsum of the Noda BiYehudah, Orach Chaim, siman 7, who wrote that regarding the pillars it is certainly [right] to permit after the taking, and the Ashkenazim practiced well; see there. However, that which appears from the words of the Nehar Shalom there, that also what the Taz permitted, s.k. 1, to hold the pillars without a covering, is [only] if the Sefer Torah is wrapped in a covering -- this is not [so]; rather it appears that the Taz permits even if the Sefer Torah is not wrapped in a covering, as is understood by one who examines [it]; and so wrote the Maamar Mordechai there. And so is implied in the responsum Shav Yaakov, siman 11, that regarding the pillars it is permitted to hold [them] without a covering; see there, and the Pischei Teshuvah and the [author of] Orach Chaim cited it, ot 2; and such appears the view of the Eliyah Rabbah, ot 1, like the view of the Taz. It turns out that there are three [views] in the matter: according to the view of the Bach, per the understanding of the Pri Chadash, even if the Sefer Torah is wrapped in a covering it is forbidden to hold the pillars without a covering; according to the view of the Pri Chadash and those who agree with him, if the Sefer Torah is wrapped in a covering it is permitted to hold the pillars without a covering; and according to the view of the Taz and those who agree with him, even if the Sefer Torah is not wrapped in a covering it is permitted to hold the pillars without a covering. And see the Noda BiYehudah there, siman 8, who wrote that one who wishes to be stringent not to touch the pillar of a Sefer Torah except with the interposition of a tallis is permitted [to do so], provided that it be in private; see there, and the Machazik Berachah cited him, ot 3, and in his sefer Ledovid Emes, siman 3, ot 10, and the rest of the later authorities. However, from the aforementioned words of the Bach it appears that since there is a dispute in this, one who wishes to be stringent -- there is no [concern of] haughtiness in it, and on the contrary it is proper to do so; and so wrote [the author] above in siman 146, ot 22, in the name of the Pesach HaDvir; see there. And the custom of the Sefardim is to make a case for the Sefer Torah made of wood and coated with silk or with silver, and when they raise the Sefer Torah to show the writing to the people they hold the case and raise [it], and at the time of the reading they hold the covering, as stated above in siman 139, ot 24, in the name of the Arizal, of blessed memory; see there.
3) There: Without a covering. The explanation is that washing the hands does not suffice. Olas Tamid, ot 2; and it is from what the Beis Yosef wrote in the name of the Agudah, whose words we brought in the previous ot, that even close to the washing it is said [to be forbidden] to hold a bare Sefer Torah; and so is the view of the Rama, of blessed memory, in the gloss, who wrote 'and with a Sefer Torah even in such a case it is forbidden' -- meaning that washing the hands is of no avail. And so wrote the Levush. And the view of Maran, of blessed memory, is that even to hold the pillars, washing the hands does not suffice, as he wrote in the Beis Yosef, and we brought his words in the previous ot, where he wrote on the words of the Mordechai, 'and it is possible that upon this the Ashkenazim rely, who hold a bare Sefer Torah at the time that they raise [it],' etc.; and the raising of the Ashkenazim is by the pillars, because they do not have the custom to make a wooden case for the Sefer Torah as the Sefardim do; and since he said 'upon this the Ashkenazim rely,' it is implied that he himself does not hold so. And so is the view of the Levush, that also to hold the pillars, washing the hands does not suffice, only if the Sefer Torah is wrapped in a covering.
4) There: Bare, without a covering. And I have heard that there are those who explain that this 'bare' does not refer to the Sefer Torah but to the person holding the Sefer Torah, that if he is bare of a fringed garment he is buried bare. Mahar"t Mildola, of blessed memory, in the sefer Mayim Rabbim, Yoreh De'ah, siman 53; Yad Aharon [in the] Mishnah Berurah, in the Hagahos HaTur, ot 1. And further see the Maamar Mordechai, ot 2, who wrote that there are those who explained 'bare' as referring to the person, that a person who is bare should not hold the Sefer Torah, and they rejected their words, and he wrote that all the poskim wrote like the words of Maran, of blessed memory, that 'bare' refers to the Sefer Torah without a covering; see there. And the practical difference is that it is proper to be stringent also according to the 'some explain,' even though according to the law we rule like the words of Maran, of blessed memory, and like the agreement of all the poskim, that 'bare' refers to the Sefer Torah. And so wrote the Yafeh LaLev, ot 1, that this matter provides support for what the Rav Ma'aseh Avraham wrote, Orach Chaim, siman 36, that one should not ascend and read from the Sefer Torah, nor perform any mitzvah connected to the Sefer Torah, without being adorned in his garment, with a tallis on his head, etc.; however, he wrote there that one should not hold back the mitzvah on account of this; see there.
5) There, gloss: And some say that the same applies to other holy writings. So wrote the Tosafos in Shabbos, folio 14a, that it is somewhat implied that it is not specifically a Sefer Torah, for all the holy writings we learned in Maseches Yadayim (chapter 3) that they render the hands impure. End of its language. And the Magen Avraham wrote, s.k. 1: and if so, also the straps of the tefillin, and all the more so the tefillin themselves, it is forbidden to hold bare, for they render the hands impure. However, in Chagigah, folio 24b, the Tosafos wrote that the straps of the tefillin together with the tefillin -- the [law] of Rabbi Parnach does not apply, etc.; and so wrote the Rosh in Maseches Yadayim; and if so, it is implied that it is permitted to hold them bare. However, [regarding] holy writings, [this is] specifically when they are written in Ashuris on leather and with ink, as stated in the Mishnah (there, chapter 4); and so wrote the Rambam (chapter 9 of Hilchos Avos HaTumah). However, [regarding] a Megillah that is written according to its law, one must be careful, for from the fact that the Rambam [stated it] without qualification, we learn that we do not rule like Shmuel (Megillah 7a), who said that Esther does not render the hands impure. End of his words. And so wrote the Mor U'Ketziah in siman 691, that the Megillah of Esther requires a covering, as stated in 'Chelek,' folio 100a; and the Machazik Berachah cited him there, ot 3. And so it is written in the sefer HaEshkol, laws of Talmud Torah, siman 12, that it is forbidden to hold the Megillah bare; see there. However, the Radbaz, part 2, siman 11, wrote that this is according to the one who explains that 'bare' refers to the person, but according to the one who explains that it refers to the Sefer Torah, the other holy writings are permitted to hold when they are bare; and the Knesses HaGedolah cited him in the Hagahos Beis Yosef and wrote 'and so the people practice.' And likewise in the responsum Shav Yaakov, Orach Chaim, siman 11, he elaborated on this matter, and concluded at the end that the other holy writings are permitted to hold when they are bare, like the words of the Radbaz, of blessed memory; see there, and the Yad Aharon in the Mishnah Berurah in the Hagahos Beis Yosef cited him, ot 1; Birkei Yosef, ot 1. And so wrote the Eliyah Rabbah, ot 1, that what the Rama said, that they did not have the custom to be stringent with holy writings, can be explained as referring to a Megillah, for with our other sefarim it is always permitted. And so it is written in the responsum Panim Me'iros, part 1, siman 76, that the world is not careful to hold a Megillah bare, and they have that upon which to rely; and the Machazik Berachah cited him, ot 4; see there. Zechor L'Avraham, ot 40. And see below, ot 7.
6) And the Radbaz wrote further there that according to all the explanations, the Oral Torah [sefarim] are permitted to hold, whether when he [the person] is bare or when they are bare; and the Knesses HaGedolah cited him there. And see the Eliyah Rabbah there, who wrote that one should be stringent even with our sefarim when it is known that his hands are soiled; see there. And according to this, also with sefarim of the Oral Torah one should be stringent not to hold them when his hands are soiled.
7) There, in the gloss: And they did not practice so. The explanation is that even with those that are written in Ashuris on leather and with ink, such as a Megillah, [they did not practice to be stringent], as is implied from the plain [reading] of the words of the Rama, of blessed memory; and so wrote the Eliyah Rabbah, ot 1, and we brought his words above in ot 5; and so it is written in the responsum Panim Me'iros, part 1, siman 76; and so it is written in the Biur HaGra; and not like the Magen Avraham, s.k. 1. And the reason that they did not practice so, one can say, is because the Tosafos wrote 'it is somewhat implied that it is not specifically a Sefer Torah,' as stated above in ot 5, and the Gemara in the chapter 'Chelek' (Sanhedrin, folio 100a) can also be explained in another way. And nonetheless, we have already written above in ot 5 that there is a dispute in this, and therefore it is proper to be stringent to hold the Megillah at the time of the reading with a garment or with its pillar, or at least not to divert his attention from the washing [of the hands], as the Rama, of blessed memory, wrote; and specifically regarding the other holy writings one may be lenient [with just] not diverting his attention from the washing, but for holding a Sefer Torah without a covering one should not be lenient [with just] washing, as the Rama, of blessed memory, wrote, and as [the author] wrote above in ot 3; see there.
8) There, in the gloss: And it is good to be stringent if he did not wash his hands. It appears to me [that this refers] to hands generally [unwashed], for we are concerned lest he touched a soiled place; and the reason that washing the hands is of avail for the other holy writings is because the Mordechai is lenient even with a Sefer Torah, as stated above in ot 2, and the Tosafos wrote 'it is somewhat implied that it is not specifically a Sefer Torah,' as [stated] in the previous ot; and therefore the Rama, of blessed memory, wrote by way of compromise that for holy writings washing the hands suffices, but not for a Sefer Torah; and examine it well.

mechaber.he: יכול מי שירצה לקנות להושיט המעילין להגולל ואין הגולל יכול למחות בו כי אף על פי שקנה הגלילה לא קנה ליקח המעילים: [וכן במקומות הנוהגין לקנות הוצאה והכנסה אין הש"ץ יכול למחות כי אין זה שייך לחזנים] [מרדכי סוף מגילה וא"ז:
mechaber.en: Anyone who wants, may purchase [the privilege] of handing the covers to the one who rolls [the Torah scroll], and the one rolling may not protest because even though [the latter] purchased the [privilege of] rolling, [the latter] did not purchase [the privilege] of the taking of the covers. (And similarly, in those places that practice to purchase [the privilege] of removing and returning [the Torah from/to the ark], the prayer leader may not protest, because that [privilege] does not belong to chazzanim). (Mordechai - end of Tractate Megillah; and Ohr Zaruah)

beur_hagra.he: ס"ב יכול כו'. כמ"ש בפ"ה דפסחים נותנו לחבירו כו' ומאי קמ"ל ברוב עם כו' ואף שזכה בו הראשון כ"ש בכה"ג:
beur_hagra.en: The U.S. can be called. As a result of the the Master’s Prayer, we will be given to Him as a result of Heaven’s mercy, and Heaven’s mercy, and that He will be the first of them

chatam_sofer.he: <small>שם במג"א ס"ק י"א </small>בבת אחת בעזרה. נ"ב עיין חמד משה ובס' מחצית השקל דשניהם קראו תימה על דברי המג"א הלא יש. לכהן שני ידים דיוכל להשקות כל אחת ביד א' ודחקו מאוד. ולפענ"ד פשוט דכוונתו דע"כ אינו משקה שתיהן בבת אחת כיון דקודם להשקאה הושבעו דא"א בבת אחת דבודאי אסור לשנות מיחיד לרבים דכתיב יתן ה' אותך וכדומה ואין יכול לומר אתכם הגם דבכל לשון נאמרה כמפורש במתני' ר"פ אלו דברים היינו לתרגם אותו לשון דכתיבה אבל לשנות מיחיד לרבים בודאי אסור וכי כן ממילא אינו משקה בב"א כנ"ל [מהגאון כתב סופר]:
chatam_sofer.en: There is a name in Heaven at once in help. Heaven’s Word tells Moses and Moses that they are not in the world. Serve two hands enough And every single one in hand is very pressured. And the Gemara is not a drink of them all at once One beard must not be changed from one to many, and Heaven will give you and the like, and you cannot tell you that the the Master is spoken in every tongue And things would have been to translate it into a written language, but to change from one to many is certainly forbidden and that is no drink in the Gemara :

levushei_serad.he: <small>שם</small> והב"ח מפרש הב"ח מתרץ קושיות הד"מ על הב"י:
levushei_serad.en: Heaven’s Word tells us that Heaven’s Word is in His Word

magen_avraham.he: כי אין זה שייך להחזן. בשלמא אם לא היה יכול לקרות בתורה אלא הש"ץ הוא היה זוכה בהוצאה אבל מעשים בכל יום שא' מתפלל וא' קורא וכו' (מרדכי):
magen_avraham.en: For this does not belong to the chazzan. If no one other than the chazzan could read from the Torah, he would indeed be entitled to the privilege of taking it out. In ordinary practice, however, one person leads the prayers and another reads from the Torah. Mordechai.

mishnah_berurah.he: (טו) כי אין זה וכו' - אבל החזן מוליכו לבימה:
mishnah_berurah.en: (15) For this is not, etc. — but the chazzan brings it to the bimah.

peri_megadim.he: גדול עט״ז הש״ע פסק כפי׳ הב׳ בטור עשרה ששייכים לקריאה והאידנא ליכא מתורגמן כבסי׳ קמ״ה ליכא בשבת רק ט׳ וא״י למה כתב סתם שקראו הא הש״ץ שייך לזה שהוא הסגן. ועיין פרישה הקשה הא גדול שבקוראים הוא גדול שבביה״כ כבסי׳ קל״ו ותי׳ שלא היה הגדול בביה״כ או לא סידר הפרשה:
peri_megadim.en: The greatest — Ateret Zekenim: Shulchan Aruch ruled per the second explanation in Tur: ten [people] associated with reading; and nowadays there is no translator, as in siman 145; on Shabbat there are only nine; and I do not know why he wrote plainly "those who read" — behold, the prayer leader is related to this, for he is the segan. And see Perishah, who questioned: behold, the greatest among those who read is the greatest in the synagogue, as in siman 136; or [perhaps] the greatest was not in the synagogue, or he did not arrange the parasha.

yad_ephraim.he: (מ"א ס"ק י"א) ודאמרי' כו' ר"ל דנראה מזה דאע"ג דהמחתה הוא הושט' האש להקטיר עליו קטורת קטורת גופ' עדיפ' ליה אע"ג דעבודת המחתה הוא קודם להקטרה לא אמרינן בכי הא אין מעבירין על המצות כיון שרוצה לעשות עיקר המצוה וה"נ אף על גב דהושט' המעילין היא קודם שיגלול מותר לו לכבד זה לאחר ולהניח לעצמו מצוה המאוחרת לה וזה כוונת המג"א במ"ש מי שנותנין לו להגביה ולגלול כו' אבל כשמכבדים אותו כו' לכאורה הך אבל אינו מובן שאינו דבר והיפוכו ולפי מ"ש נראה כוונתו דבענין הגבהה וגלילה שפיר יש לו לתפוס מצוה הקודמ' דהיינו הגבהה ולא מטעם קדימה רק מטעם שהיא עיקר המצוה אבל מי שמכבדין להושיט כו' גליל' עדיפא אע"פ שהיא מאוחרת כיון שהיא עיקר המצוה אמנם המג"א כתב שאין מוכרח ולכן הוצרך להביא ראיה ממחתה:
yad_ephraim.en: (Magen Avraham note 11) And we say, etc. — meaning: it appears from this that even though the coal pan was handed — fire to burn incense upon it — the incense itself is preferable to him even though the work of the coal pan precedes the burning; we do not say in such a case one does not pass over mitzvot, since he wants to do the essence of the mitzvah; and similarly even though handing the mantles precedes rolling, he is permitted to honor this one later and leave for himself the later mitzvah — and this is Magen Avraham's intent in what he wrote "one to whom they give to lift and to roll," etc.; but when they honor him, etc. — at first glance this contradicts, but it is not understood that it is not a matter and its opposite; and per what he wrote, his intent appears: regarding lifting and rolling it is fine for him to take the prior mitzvah — that is lifting — not because of precedence but because it is the essence of the mitzvah; but one whom they honor to hand — rolling is preferable even though it is later, since it is the essence of the mitzvah. However Magen Avraham wrote it is not necessary, and therefore he had to bring proof from the coal pan.

kaf_hachayyim.he: ב) שם אסור לאחוז ס"ת ערום וכו' כתב ב"י דהמרדכי כתב דה"מ בידים סתם אבל נטל ולא הסיח דעתו לא קפדינן ע"כ וכתב ב"י ואפשר שע"ז סומכין האשכנזים שאוחזין ס"ת ערום בשעה שמגביהין אותו להראות הכתב לעם ומיהו מצאתי כתוב בשם אגודה דאפי' סמוך לנטילה קאמר עכ"ל מיהו מור"ם ז"ל בד"מ או' ב' כתב דאני מבני בניהם ולא ראיתי מנהג זה ביניהם אלא אדרבא נזהרין שלא ליגע בס"ת ערום אבל בשאר כתבי קודש אין נזהרין כלל ולא ראיתי מימי מי שחשש לזה בשאר ספרים עכ"ל והב"ח כתב ע"ז דאסור לאחוז ערום וכו' פי' הקורא בתירה צריך לאחוז בעמודי התורה בשעת ברכה וקורא כדלעיל סס"י קל"ט ואסור לו לאחוז בעמודי הספר בלא מטפחת ומנהג שלנו שאין נזהרין בזה סומכין על מ"ש המרדכי ע"ש ראבי"ה בסוף מגילה דה"מ בידים סתם אבל נטל ולא הסיח דעתו לא קפדינן וכו' וסיים דכל ירא שמים לא יאחז בעמודי ס"ת ערום בלי מטפחת וכן ראיתי מן המדקדקים דבין בשעה שקירין בין בשעה שמגביהין אוחזין בעמודי ס"ת ע"י כנף הטלית ושמעתי שכך נוהגין במדינת אשכנז ונכון הוא עכ"ל וכן דעת המ"א בריש הסי' דאפי' בעמודים אסור לאחוז ערום יעו"ש. וכתב הפר"ח או' א' דמדברי הב"ח יראה דאפי' כרוך במטפחת אסור לו לאחוז בעמודי הספר בלא מטפחת או ע"י כנף הטלית וליתא דנהי דכשהוא ערום אסור לאחוז בעמודיו וכמו שדקדק מוהרי"ט ח"א סי' קל"ו מדברי הרמב"ם וכ"נ מדברי הב"י אבל כשהוא כרוך במטפחת פשיטא דשרי לאחיז בעמודי הספר אפי' בלא מטפחת עכ"ל וכ"כ י"א בהגב"י מיהו הנה"ש או' א' כתב דאם הס"ת כרוך במטפחת לכ"ע שרי לאחיז בעמודים בלא מטפחת ומ"ש הב"י שהאשכנזים אוחזים ס"ת ערום בשעה שמגביהין וכו' היינו שהיו אוחזין אותו בלי מטפחת סביבו יעו"ש. וכ"כ המאמ"ר או' א' דאם הס"ת כרוך במטפחת מותר לאחוז בעמודים בלא מטפחת יעו"ש. וכ"כ המש"ז או' א' וא"א בריש הסי' יעו"ש. ועיין בתשו' ניב"י חא"ח סי' ז' שכתב דבעמודים ודאי שיש להתיר אחר הנטילה ויפה נהגו בני אשכנז יעו"ש אמנם מה שנראה מדברי הנה"ש שם דגם מה שהתיר הט"ז סק"א לאחוז בעמודים בלא מטפחת היינו אם הס"ת כרוך במטפחת ליתא אלא נראה שהט"ז מתיר אפי' אם אין הס"ת כרוך במטפחת כמובן למעיין וכ"כ המאמ"ר שם. וכ"מ בתשו' שב יעקב סי' י"א דבעמודים מותר לאחוז בלי מטפחת יע"ש והביאו פ"ת וא"ח או' ב' וכ"נ דעת הא"ר או' א' כדעת הט"ז. נמצא דג' מחלוקות בדבר דלדעת הב"ח לפי הבנת הפר"ח אפי' אם הס"ת כרובה במטפחת אסור לאחוז בעמודים בלא מטפחת ולדעת הפר"ח ודעמיה אם הס"ת כרוכה במטפחת מותר לאחוז בעמודים בלא מטפחת ולדעת הט"ז ודעמיה אפי' אין הס"ת כרוכה במטפחת מותר לאחוז בעמודים בלא מטפחת. ועיין בנוב"י שם סי' ח' שכתב דהרוצה להחמיר שלא ליגע בעמוד ס"ת אלא בהפסקת טלית רשאי ובלבד שיהיה בצנעה יעו"ש והביאו מחב"ר או' ג' ובספרו לד"א סי' ג' או' יו"ד ושאר אחרונים מיהו מדברי הב"ח הנ"ז כראה כיון דאיכא בזה פלוגתא הרוצה להחמיר אין בו משום יוהרא ואדרבא נכון לעשות כן וכ"כ לעיל סי' קמ"ו או' כ"ב בשם הפתה"ד יעו"ש. ומנהג הספרדים לעשות תיק לס"ת מעשה עץ ומצופה במשי או בכסף וכשמגביהין הס"ת להראות הכתיבה לעם אוחזין בתיק ומגביהין ובשעת הקריאה אוחזין במטפחת כמ"ש לעיל סי' קל"ט או כ"ד בשם האר"י ז"ל יעו"ש:
kaf_hachayyim.en: 2) There: It is forbidden to hold a bare Sefer Torah, etc. The Beis Yosef wrote that the Mordechai wrote that this applies to [holding with] bare hands generally, but if he took [it] and did not divert his attention, we are not particular. Until here. And the Beis Yosef wrote: and it is possible that upon this the Ashkenazim rely, who hold a bare Sefer Torah at the time that they raise it to show the writing to the people; however, I found written in the name of the Agudah that even close to the taking it is said [to be forbidden]. End of his language. However, the Rama, of blessed memory, in the Darkei Moshe, ot 2, wrote: I am of their descendants and I have not seen this custom among them; rather, on the contrary, they are careful not to touch a bare Sefer Torah; but with other holy writings they are not careful at all, and I have never seen anyone who was concerned about this with other sefarim. End of his language. And the Bach wrote on this 'it is forbidden to hold [it] bare,' etc.: the explanation is that the reader from the Torah must hold the pillars of the Torah at the time of the blessing and reading, as [stated] above at the end of siman 139, and it is forbidden for him to hold the pillars of the scroll without a covering; and our custom that they are not careful in this relies on what the Mordechai wrote in the name of the Ra'avyah at the end of Megillah, that this applies to [holding with] bare hands generally, but if he took [it] and did not divert his attention we are not particular, etc.; and he concluded that every God-fearing person should not hold the pillars of a bare Sefer Torah without a covering. And likewise I have seen among the meticulous that both at the time that they read and at the time that they raise [it], they hold the pillars of the Sefer Torah by means of the corner of the tallis; and I have heard that so they practice in the land of Ashkenaz, and it is proper. End of his language. And so is the view of the Magen Avraham at the beginning of the siman, that even the pillars it is forbidden to hold bare; see there. And the Pri Chadash wrote, ot 1, that from the words of the Bach it appears that even [when the scroll is] wrapped in a covering it is forbidden for him to hold the pillars of the scroll without a covering or by means of the corner of the tallis; and this is not [so], for although when it is bare it is forbidden to hold its pillars, as the Mahari"t, part 1, siman 136, inferred from the words of the Rambam, and so it appears from the words of the Beis Yosef -- but when it is wrapped in a covering, it is obvious that it is permitted to hold the pillars of the scroll even without a covering. End of his language. And so wrote the Yad Aharon in the Hagahos Beis Yosef. However, the Nehar Shalom, ot 1, wrote that if the Sefer Torah is wrapped in a covering, according to all opinions it is permitted to hold the pillars without a covering; and that which the Beis Yosef wrote, that the Ashkenazim hold a bare Sefer Torah at the time that they raise [it], etc., means that they would hold it without a covering around it; see there. And so wrote the Maamar Mordechai, ot 1, that if the Sefer Torah is wrapped in a covering it is permitted to hold the pillars without a covering; see there. And so wrote the Mishbetzos Zahav, ot 1, and the Eshel Avraham at the beginning of the siman; see there. And see the responsum of the Noda BiYehudah, Orach Chaim, siman 7, who wrote that regarding the pillars it is certainly [right] to permit after the taking, and the Ashkenazim practiced well; see there. However, that which appears from the words of the Nehar Shalom there, that also what the Taz permitted, s.k. 1, to hold the pillars without a covering, is [only] if the Sefer Torah is wrapped in a covering -- this is not [so]; rather it appears that the Taz permits even if the Sefer Torah is not wrapped in a covering, as is understood by one who examines [it]; and so wrote the Maamar Mordechai there. And so is implied in the responsum Shav Yaakov, siman 11, that regarding the pillars it is permitted to hold [them] without a covering; see there, and the Pischei Teshuvah and the [author of] Orach Chaim cited it, ot 2; and such appears the view of the Eliyah Rabbah, ot 1, like the view of the Taz. It turns out that there are three [views] in the matter: according to the view of the Bach, per the understanding of the Pri Chadash, even if the Sefer Torah is wrapped in a covering it is forbidden to hold the pillars without a covering; according to the view of the Pri Chadash and those who agree with him, if the Sefer Torah is wrapped in a covering it is permitted to hold the pillars without a covering; and according to the view of the Taz and those who agree with him, even if the Sefer Torah is not wrapped in a covering it is permitted to hold the pillars without a covering. And see the Noda BiYehudah there, siman 8, who wrote that one who wishes to be stringent not to touch the pillar of a Sefer Torah except with the interposition of a tallis is permitted [to do so], provided that it be in private; see there, and the Machazik Berachah cited him, ot 3, and in his sefer Ledovid Emes, siman 3, ot 10, and the rest of the later authorities. However, from the aforementioned words of the Bach it appears that since there is a dispute in this, one who wishes to be stringent -- there is no [concern of] haughtiness in it, and on the contrary it is proper to do so; and so wrote [the author] above in siman 146, ot 22, in the name of the Pesach HaDvir; see there. And the custom of the Sefardim is to make a case for the Sefer Torah made of wood and coated with silk or with silver, and when they raise the Sefer Torah to show the writing to the people they hold the case and raise [it], and at the time of the reading they hold the covering, as stated above in siman 139, ot 24, in the name of the Arizal, of blessed memory; see there.

mechaber.he: הגולל ספר תורה יעמידנו כנגד התפר כדי שאם יקרע יקרע התפר:
mechaber.en: The one who rolls the Torah scroll positions it at the seam [in such a way] such that if it rips, it rips the seam.

beer_hagolah.en: There's a name in the Gemara

levushei_serad.he: <small>שם</small> המשיחות והרצועות עיין בנודע ביהודה סי' ז':
levushei_serad.en: <small>There</small> “the cords and straps.” See Noda BiYehudah, siman 7.

machatzit_hashekel.he: (ס"ק ג) ורגילים כו' צ"ע כו' וצ"ל דמ"מ מי שמעלה בדמים כו אם כן שלא כדין עושין הגבאים כי לפעמים לא נמצא בבה"כ מי שקנה גלילה והגבאים מכבדים להישר בעיניהם דראוי לגבאים לכבד לגדול:
machatzit_hashekel.en: (s.k. 3) And they are accustomed, etc. — this requires study, etc.; and one must say: nevertheless, one who contributes more money, etc. — if so, the gabbaim act improperly, for sometimes there is not found in the synagogue one who bought [the privilege of] rolling, and the gabbaim honor [someone] to appear upright in their eyes; for it is fitting for gabbaim to honor the great one.

peri_megadim.he: פירוש כשהספר עט״ז עב״י האריך בפירושים והט״ז מפרש כשאחד עושה הכל הגבהה ומראה לעם ואח״כ נותן הס״ת ביד אחר לאחוז והוא גולל יהפך הכתב אליו ויתחיל להדוק המטפחת (הוא שקורין מפה) דוקא בצד חוצה לו דהיינו מאחורי הס״ת שהוא נגד האוחז הס״ת ומשם יתחיל להדק המפה ויביא אח״כ אליו נגד פניו והטעם כנרות דחנוכה בסי׳ תרע״ו אות וי״ו דכל שיש פינות תחלה וסוף יתחיל מפינת ימין אל השמאל וכמו בנר חנוכה דעתו שיתחיל בנר היותר ימיני בהתחלה ואח״כ יפנה לשמאל ה״ה כאן יתחיל בצד ימיני שלו והוא מבחוץ כו׳ ומ״ש מרמ״א כו׳ לא הבינותי כעת:
peri_megadim.en: Meaning: when the scroll — Ateret Zekenim, explicitly. Beit Yosef elaborated in the explanations, and Taz explains: when one person does everything — hagbahah and showing to the people — and afterward gives the Torah scroll into another's hand to hold, and he rolls: he turns the writing toward himself and begins to fasten the cloth (which is called a mappah) specifically on the side outside relative to him, i.e., behind the Torah scroll, which is opposite the one holding the Torah scroll; and from there he begins to fasten the cloth and afterward brings it toward him, opposite his face. And the reason is like Chanukah candles in siman 676, letter 16: whatever has corners — beginning and end — one begins from the right corner toward the left; and like the Chanukah candle, his intent is to begin with the rightmost candle at the start, and afterward turn to the left; here too he begins on his right side, and it is from outside, etc. And what Rama wrote, etc. — I did not understand now.

kaf_hachayyim.he: ג) שם. בלא מטפחת. פי' ולא סגי בנטילת ידים. עו"ת או' ב' והוא ממ"ש בב"י בשם האגודה והבאנו דבריו באו' הקודם דאפי' סמוך לנטילה קאמר דאסור לאחוז ס"ת ערום וכן הוא סברת מור"ם ז"ל בהגה שכתב ובס"ת אפי' בכה"ג אסור ור"ל דלא מהני נט"י. וכ"כ הלבוש, ודעת מר"ן ז"ל גם לאחוז בעמודים לא סגי בנט"י כמ"ש בב"י והבאנו דבריו באו' הקודם שכתב על דברי המרדכי ואפשר שע"ז סומכין האשכנזים שאוחזין ס"ת ערום בשעה שמגביהין וכו' וההגבהה של האשכנזים היא בעמודים מפני שאין נוהגין לעשות תיק של עץ לס"ת כמו שעושק הספרדים ומדקאמר ע"ז סומכיו האשכנזים משמע דלדידיה לא ס"ל הכי וכן דעת הלבוש דגם לאחוז בעמודים לא סגי בנט"י רק אם הס"ת כרוכה במטפחת:
kaf_hachayyim.en: 3) There: Without a covering. The explanation is that washing the hands does not suffice. Olas Tamid, ot 2; and it is from what the Beis Yosef wrote in the name of the Agudah, whose words we brought in the previous ot, that even close to the washing it is said [to be forbidden] to hold a bare Sefer Torah; and so is the view of the Rama, of blessed memory, in the gloss, who wrote 'and with a Sefer Torah even in such a case it is forbidden' -- meaning that washing the hands is of no avail. And so wrote the Levush. And the view of Maran, of blessed memory, is that even to hold the pillars, washing the hands does not suffice, as he wrote in the Beis Yosef, and we brought his words in the previous ot, where he wrote on the words of the Mordechai, 'and it is possible that upon this the Ashkenazim rely, who hold a bare Sefer Torah at the time that they raise [it],' etc.; and the raising of the Ashkenazim is by the pillars, because they do not have the custom to make a wooden case for the Sefer Torah as the Sefardim do; and since he said 'upon this the Ashkenazim rely,' it is implied that he himself does not hold so. And so is the view of the Levush, that also to hold the pillars, washing the hands does not suffice, only if the Sefer Torah is wrapped in a covering.

mechaber.he: הגולל ספר תורה גוללו מבחוץ וכשהוא מהדקו מהדקו מבפנים: הגה פירוש כשהספר עומד לפניו יהיה הכתב נגד פניו ויתחיל לגלול מבחוץ ואחר שגמר הגלילה יהדק סוף המטפחת בפנים שכשיבא לקרות בו ימצא ההדוק בפנים ולא יצטרך להפך הס"ת (טור והרא"ש ס"פ בני העיר) ונראה דכל זה מיירי כשאחד עושה כל הגלילה אבל עכשיו שנוהגים שאחד מגביה ואחד גולל יהיה הכתב נגד המגביה וכן נוהגים כי הוא עיקר הגולל והאוחז ס"ת:
mechaber.en: The one who rolls the Torah scroll rolls it from outside; and when one fastens it, one should fasten it from the inside. {Rama: Gloss: meaning: when the [Torah] scroll is standing before one, the writing should be opposite one's face, and one should start to roll from the outside. And after one finishes the rolling, one should fasten the end of the cloth on the inside so that when they come to read from it [the next time], they will find the fastening on the inside and they won't need to flip over the Torah scroll [to unfasten it]. (Tur and the Rosh - end of chapter "B'nei Ha-ir"). And it seems that all of this is when one person does the entire rolling [process]. But nowadays when the custom is that one person raises [the Torah] and another person rolls it, the writing should be facing the one raising it. And that is the custom, since he (ie. the one raising it) is the main "roller" and he is the one holding the Torah.}

eliyah_rabbah.en:
[5] The writing facing the one who raises it, etc. When I roll the Sefer Torah, I customarily draw the poles toward me so that the scroll remains level as it had been lying until it is completely rolled. The writing then faces me and the one who raised it. I found support for this in Shiyarei Knesses HaGedolah. It is obvious that if one is offered both raising and rolling, he should choose raising, and if he is offered rolling and handing over the mantles, he should choose rolling. See Yoma 70a, that it is a mitzvah to observe the performance of mitzvos because “In a multitude of people is the King’s glory.” Nevertheless, one may leave and go to observe another mitzvah once he is no longer engaged in the first.
[6] He should not roll, etc. Because this is degrading to the Torah. For the same reason, it appears proper to be stringent not to hold the straps of tefillin and allow the boxes to roll around the straps. Rather, one should hold the tefillin in his hand and wind the strap around them. Although the straps possess sanctity, the boxes possess greater sanctity, as explained above in siman 32. See also above, siman 10.

(יט) עיקר הגולל - משמע שהגבהה היא יותר מצוה מגלילה וע"כ מי שנותנין לו ס"ת להגביה ולגלול וא"א לו לעשות שתיהן יגביה ויתן לאחר לגלול אבל אם כיבדו אותו להושטת המעיל ולגלול הגלילה עדיפא דהיא עיקר המצוה ויתן לאחר להושיט:

(16) Meaning: when the scroll, etc. — meaning that one should not err to interpret what they said, "he rolls it from outside," [as meaning that] when he holds the atzei chayim of the Torah scroll to show the writing to the people, he compresses his hold in a manner that its back is toward him; and automatically, when he wants to roll, the rolling too will be only behind the scroll, for the writing is not facing his face. And therefore it teaches us that it is not so: even though it is a mitzvah to show the writing to the people, as stated in Massekhet Soferim, nevertheless the writing must be facing the face of the one holding the Torah scroll — so at the time of hagbahah, and so at the time of rolling; for since he is engaged with the Torah scroll, the honor of the Torah is that the writing be facing his face. And what they said, "he rolls it from outside," means that the beginning of the rolling should be from outside, as we will explain in the s.k. after this.
(17) And he shall begin to roll — meaning: the beginning of placing the cloth on the Torah scroll to roll it should be from outside; and see Machatzit HaShekel, who tends to say that this is specifically per what Rama concludes, that it speaks when the one who raises also does the rolling; and therefore we are concerned that if the rolling begins from the side of the inside, one must be concerned, Heaven forbid, that the Torah scroll fall toward the outside [unlike when he begins from outside, for it is impossible that it fall outward, for he holds it with the cloth with which he begins to roll around it]. But per our custom, where one raises and the second rolls, there is no need to be so concerned that it will fall; for since the one rolling stands before the Torah scroll, it cannot fall quickly and he will not notice. It is possible that if he wishes he may begin to roll it from the side of the inside; and such is our custom — we are not particular about this.

It means on the SAT. When he comes to roll, he will turn the face of the handkerchief to himself and then to the person holding it, which is not our custom, and he will begin to roll the handkerchief on the outside of the handkerchief and wrap that side all over, and then face the face of the handkerchief, that is, against the scroller to the apoki, if he wants to roll, first the entire inner side and then the outer side, all the corners should be to the right, that is, he should start on the right side and turn to the left, as in Hanukkah candles, per the above, correct I did not interpret it per the taste, except that from the words of the Rama 27, 17, Demeiri in one does the whole scroll, which means that he did not interpret it according to our interpretations, and the next day I wrote:

kaf_hachayyim.he: ד) שם. ערום בלא מטפחת. ואני שמעתי שיש מפרשים דהאי ערום לא קאי אס"ת אלא על האדם האוחז ס"ת שאם הוא ערום מטלית מצוייץ נקבר ערום. מהר"ט מילדולה ז"ל בספר מים רבים חי"ד סי' נ"ג, י"א מ"ב בהגה"ט או' א' ועוד עיין מאמ"ר או' ב' שכתב שיש שפירשו ערום על האדם דאדם שהוא ערום לא יאחוז בס"ת ודחו דבריהם וכתב דכל הפו' כתבו כדברי מר"ן ז"ל דערום על הס"ת בלא מטפחת יעו"ש. ונ"מ דנכון להחמיר גם לפי יש מפרשים אע"ג דלפום דינא ק"ל כדברי מר"ן ז"ל וכהסכמת כל הפו' דערום קאי אס"ת. וכ"כ היפ"ל או' א' דהני מילי סיועי מסייע' ליה למ"ש הרב מעשה אברהם חא"ח סי' ל"ו דאין לעלות ולקרות בס"ת וגם לעשות שום מצוה הנוגע לס"ת בלתי הדור בלבושו בטלית על ראשו וכו' מיהו כתב שם אבל אין לעכב המצוה בשביל זה יעו"ש:
kaf_hachayyim.en: 4) There: Bare, without a covering. And I have heard that there are those who explain that this 'bare' does not refer to the Sefer Torah but to the person holding the Sefer Torah, that if he is bare of a fringed garment he is buried bare. Mahar"t Mildola, of blessed memory, in the sefer Mayim Rabbim, Yoreh De'ah, siman 53; Yad Aharon [in the] Mishnah Berurah, in the Hagahos HaTur, ot 1. And further see the Maamar Mordechai, ot 2, who wrote that there are those who explained 'bare' as referring to the person, that a person who is bare should not hold the Sefer Torah, and they rejected their words, and he wrote that all the poskim wrote like the words of Maran, of blessed memory, that 'bare' refers to the Sefer Torah without a covering; see there. And the practical difference is that it is proper to be stringent also according to the 'some explain,' even though according to the law we rule like the words of Maran, of blessed memory, and like the agreement of all the poskim, that 'bare' refers to the Sefer Torah. And so wrote the Yafeh LaLev, ot 1, that this matter provides support for what the Rav Ma'aseh Avraham wrote, Orach Chaim, siman 36, that one should not ascend and read from the Sefer Torah, nor perform any mitzvah connected to the Sefer Torah, without being adorned in his garment, with a tallis on his head, etc.; however, he wrote there that one should not hold back the mitzvah on account of this; see there.

mechaber.he: מוטב תגלל המטפחת סביב הס"ת ולא יגלול הס"ת כשכורכו במטפחת:
mechaber.en: It is better to wrap the cloth around the Torah scroll rather than to wrap the Torah scroll by rolling it around the cloth.

baer_heitev.he: הס"ת. פי' שלא יאחוז המפה בידו ויגלול הס"ת סביבו:
baer_heitev.en: The S. He will not give up the map in his hand, and he will be cursed around him:

levushei_serad.he: <small>ט"ז סק"ג</small> פירושו המטפחת. ר"ל דתיבת לגלול פירושו לכרוך המטפחת:
levushei_serad.en: <small>Taz, seif katan 3</small> “Its meaning is the cloth.” Meaning, the word “to roll” means to wrap the cloth around it.

machatzit_hashekel.he:
(ס"ק ה) מדברים כו' ומיהו בתשובת מהרי"ל כ' כו' שכ' תחלה דאין לעשות תשמישי ס"ת מבגד שנשתמש בו הדיוט וסיים ואף דנהוג עלמא לעשות מפות ופרוכת מבגדים ישנים לאו מר בריה דרבינא חתים עליה עכ"ל הרי דגם על פרוכת כ' דלאו' בריה דרבינא חתום עליה משמע דגם פרוכת דעתו לאסור מצד הדין:
ומיהו העולם נוהגים כו' וכמ"ש מהרי"ל אבל מהרי"ל לא הסכים עם המנהג כצ"ל:
ונ"ל דס"ל כו' רצה ליישב המנהג שלא יהיה נגד התוספת':
דהרי הכיור כו' בספר א"ר הקשה דה"ל להביא ראיה מחח ונזם וכומז ולפנ"ד דמהני אין ראיה כיון דהותכו א"כ ודאי פנים חדשו' באו לכאן משא"כ לעשות מבגדים ישנים אף שמשתנה עכשיו כלי אחר מ"מ צורת הבגד עדיין עליו דהיינו צורה הראשונ' א"א ללמוד התירו מחח ונזם דהותכו באש אף דמ"מ נשאר זהב כבתחלה מ"מ ע"י היתוך אש נשתנ' שינוי גמור לכן אייתי ראי' ממראות הצובאות שלא נשתנו אלא מאותן מראות גופייהו נעש' כיור ולא הותכו תחלה באש אלא נעשה ממנו כלי אחר דומה שפיר לבגדים ישנים שעושין מהן תשמיש קדוש' וכן מצאתי בתשו' חות יאיר:
ואע"ג דבמזבח בעי' עצים כו' זה ראיית האוסרין מדאמרי' במנחות דף כ"ב ע"ב. כתיב על העצים אשר על האש אשר על המזבח מה מזבח משל צבור אף עצים ואש משל צבור ולא משל יחיד דברי ר"א בר"ש ר"א בן שמוע או' מה מזבח שלא נשתמש בו הדיוט אף עצים ואש שלא נשתמש בו הדיוט ופסק הרמב"ם בהל' איסורי מזבח כר"א בן שמוע עיין בברכת הזבח הטעם דפסק כוותיה ומזה למדו דה"ה לתשמישי ס"ת בעי' דבר שלא נשתמש בו הדיוט:
וכ"מ בגמ' ר"ל דהא דאיצטריך היקשא לעצים ואש למזבח לאסור עצים ואש שנשתמש בו הדיוט משמע אי לאו היקשא לא הוי ילפי' בבנין אב עצים ואש ממזבח דבעי' שלא נשתמש בו הדיוט וא"כ ה"ה השתא דאיכא היקשא לעצים ואש לא ילפי' מיניה תשמישי ס"ת דמה לעצים ואש דדומ' יותר למזבח דתרווייהו ענייני בהמ"ק הם ואפ"ה לולי היקשא לא הוי ילפינן ממזבח כ"ש דאין ללמוד בבנין אב תשמישי ס"ת דאין דומה לבנין בהמ"ק אלא אמרי' מה דגלי גלי ותו לא:
machatzit_hashekel.en:
(s.k. 5) From old materials, etc. — however, in the responsum of Maharil he wrote, etc., that he wrote at first that one should not make implements of a Torah scroll from a garment that a commoner used, and concluded; and even though the world is accustomed to make cloths and a curtain from old garments — "not the son of Ravina signed on it" — until here; behold, that on a curtain too he wrote "not the son of Ravina signed on it," which implies that on a curtain too his view is to forbid from the perspective of law.
However, the world practices, etc., as Maharil wrote; but Maharil did not agree with the custom, as should be read.
And it appears to me that he holds, etc. — he wanted to settle the custom so that it would not be against Tosafot.
For the basin, etc. — in Sefer Or Zarua he questioned that one should bring proof from a spoon, ring, and pomander; and per my humble opinion, since they were melted, there is no proof, since they were melted; if so, certainly "new faces came here," unlike making from old garments — even though now it is a different implement, nevertheless the form of the garment is still upon it, i.e., the initial shape; one cannot learn permission from spoon and ring that were melted in fire, even though nevertheless gold remained as at first — nevertheless through melting by fire there was a complete change; therefore he brought proof from the mirrors of the midwives, which were not melted first in fire, but from those mirrors themselves a [different] implement was made — the basin; and they were not melted first in fire, but an other implement similar [was made] from them — fine [analogy] to old garments from which one makes holy implements; and so I found in responsum Chavat Yair.
And even though on the altar wood is required, etc. — this is the proof of those who forbid, from what we say in Menachot daf 22b: it is written "upon the wood that is on the fire that is on the altar" — just as the altar [belongs to] the congregation, so too wood and fire [belong to] the congregation and not to an individual — the words of R' Eliezer in the name of R' Shimon; R' Eliezer ben Shimon says: just as the altar was not used by a commoner, so too wood and fire that were not used by a commoner; and Rambam ruled in Laws of Forbidden Offerings like R' Eliezer ben Shimon — see Berakhat HaZevach the reason he ruled like him; and from this they learned that the same applies to implements of a Torah scroll: one requires something that was not used by a commoner.
And so in the Gemara — meaning that the derivation was needed for wood and fire to the altar to forbid wood and fire that a commoner used; it implies that if not for the derivation, one would not derive by binyan av wood and fire from the altar, which requires that a commoner not have used it; and if so, now that there is a derivation for wood and fire, one does not derive from it implements of a Torah scroll — for what [comparison] to wood and fire, which are more similar to the altar, for both are matters of the Beit HaMikdash? And nevertheless, without the derivation one would not derive from the altar; all the more so one does not derive by binyan av implements of a Torah scroll, which are not similar to implements of the Beit HaMikdash; rather we say: what was revealed, was revealed, and no more.

magen_avraham.he: ולא יגלול. פי' שלא יאחז המפה בידו ויגלול הס"ת סביבו:
magen_avraham.en: He should not roll. Meaning, he should not hold the cloth in his hand and roll the Sefer Torah around it.

mishnah_berurah.he: (כ) ולא יגלול - פי' שלא יאחוז המפה בידו ויגלול הס"ת סביבו דאינו כבוד לתורה:
mishnah_berurah.en: (b) And he shall not be cursed, for he shall not give up the map in his hand, and shall not be cursed by the Almighty

kaf_hachayyim.he: ה) שם הגה. וי"א דה"ה שאר כתבי הקודש. כ"כ התוס' בשבת דף י"ד ע"א דקצת משמע דלאו דוקא ס"ת דהא כל כתבי הקודש תנן במס' ידים (פ"ג) שמטמאין את הידים עכ"ל וכתב המ"א סק"א וא"כ גם רצועות התפילין וכ"ש בתפילין עצמן אסור לאחוז ערום דהרי מטמאין הידים ומיהו בחגיגה דכ"ד ע"ב כתבו התוס' דרצועות של תפילין עם התפילין לא שייך דרבי פרנך וכו' וכ"כ הרא"ש במס' ידים וא"כ משמע דמותר לאוחזן ערום. ומיהו כתבי קידש דוקא כשכתובין אשורית על העור ובדיו כדאיתא במשנה (שם פ"ד) וכ"כ הרמב"ם (פ"ט מהלכות אבות הטומאה) ומיהו במגילה שכתובה כדינה צריך ליזהר דמסתם הרמב"ם ש"מ דלא ק"ל כשמואל (מגילה ז' ע"א) דאמר אסתר אינה מטמאה ידים עכ"ד וכ"כ המו"ק בסי' תרצ"א דמגילת אסתר בעיא מטפחת כדאיתא בחלק דף ק' ע"א. והביאו מחב"ר שם או' ג' וכ"כ בס' האשכול ה' ת"ת סי' י"ב דאסור לאחוז המגילה ערום יעו"ש. מיהו בהרדב"ז ת"ב סי' י"א כתב דזה למאן דמפרש דערום קאי אאדם אבל למאן דמפרש דקאי לס"ת שאר כתבי הקודש מותר לאחזן כשהן ערומים, והביאו כנה"ג בהגב"י וכתב וכן עמא דבר, וכן בתשו' שב יעקב חאו"ח סי' י"א האריך בענין זה ולבסוף מסיק דשאר כתבי הקודש מותר לאוחזן כשהן ערומים וכדברי הרדב"ז ז"ל יעו"ש והביאו י"א במ"ב בהגב"י או' א' ברכ"י או' א' וכ"כ א"ר או' א' דמ"ש רמ"א דלא נהגו להחמיר בכתבי הקודש י"ל דקאי אמגילה דבשאר ספרים שלנו לעולם מותר. וכ"כ בתשו' פנים מאירות ח"א סי' ע"ו דהעולם אין נזהרין לאחוז מגילה ערומה ויש להם על מה שיסמוכו. והביאו מחב"ר או ד' יעו"ש. זכ"ל או' מ' ועיין לקמן או' ז'
kaf_hachayyim.en: 5) There, gloss: And some say that the same applies to other holy writings. So wrote the Tosafos in Shabbos, folio 14a, that it is somewhat implied that it is not specifically a Sefer Torah, for all the holy writings we learned in Maseches Yadayim (chapter 3) that they render the hands impure. End of its language. And the Magen Avraham wrote, s.k. 1: and if so, also the straps of the tefillin, and all the more so the tefillin themselves, it is forbidden to hold bare, for they render the hands impure. However, in Chagigah, folio 24b, the Tosafos wrote that the straps of the tefillin together with the tefillin -- the [law] of Rabbi Parnach does not apply, etc.; and so wrote the Rosh in Maseches Yadayim; and if so, it is implied that it is permitted to hold them bare. However, [regarding] holy writings, [this is] specifically when they are written in Ashuris on leather and with ink, as stated in the Mishnah (there, chapter 4); and so wrote the Rambam (chapter 9 of Hilchos Avos HaTumah). However, [regarding] a Megillah that is written according to its law, one must be careful, for from the fact that the Rambam [stated it] without qualification, we learn that we do not rule like Shmuel (Megillah 7a), who said that Esther does not render the hands impure. End of his words. And so wrote the Mor U'Ketziah in siman 691, that the Megillah of Esther requires a covering, as stated in 'Chelek,' folio 100a; and the Machazik Berachah cited him there, ot 3. And so it is written in the sefer HaEshkol, laws of Talmud Torah, siman 12, that it is forbidden to hold the Megillah bare; see there. However, the Radbaz, part 2, siman 11, wrote that this is according to the one who explains that 'bare' refers to the person, but according to the one who explains that it refers to the Sefer Torah, the other holy writings are permitted to hold when they are bare; and the Knesses HaGedolah cited him in the Hagahos Beis Yosef and wrote 'and so the people practice.' And likewise in the responsum Shav Yaakov, Orach Chaim, siman 11, he elaborated on this matter, and concluded at the end that the other holy writings are permitted to hold when they are bare, like the words of the Radbaz, of blessed memory; see there, and the Yad Aharon in the Mishnah Berurah in the Hagahos Beis Yosef cited him, ot 1; Birkei Yosef, ot 1. And so wrote the Eliyah Rabbah, ot 1, that what the Rama said, that they did not have the custom to be stringent with holy writings, can be explained as referring to a Megillah, for with our other sefarim it is always permitted. And so it is written in the responsum Panim Me'iros, part 1, siman 76, that the world is not careful to hold a Megillah bare, and they have that upon which to rely; and the Machazik Berachah cited him, ot 4; see there. Zechor L'Avraham, ot 40. And see below, ot 7.

mechaber.he: הגולל ס"ת בתוך התיק טועה:
mechaber.en: One who rolls the Torah scroll while it is in it's case/pouch is making a mistake.

beur_hagra.he: הגולל כו'. שמ"ש בסוף מגילה גולל מבחוץ פירוש דהיינו חוץ לתיק ריב"ש סי' ל"ב ועט"ז ועריב"ש סי' ז':
beur_hagra.en: The one who rolls, etc. What is stated at the end of Megillah, that he rolls it from the outside, means from outside the case. Rivash, siman 32. See Taz, and see Rivash, siman 7.

levushei_serad.he: <small>מ"א סק"ז</small> דדוק' קאמר. משום דאהא דמהדק סוף המטפחת בפנים יהיב רמ"א טעמא שלא יצטרך להפך הס"ת ואהא דיתחיל לגלול פי' לכרוך המפה מבחוץ לא יהיב טעמא ה"א דהכי קאמר שמותר לגלול מחוץ אם ירצה משא"כ ההידוק דוקא מבפנים מש"ה כתב המג"א דמשמע דהך נמי דוקא הוא משום חשש שתפול ח"ו:
levushei_serad.en: <small>Magen Avraham, seif katan 7</small> “He means this specifically.” Rama gives a reason for fastening the end of the cloth on the inside, namely, so that one will not need to turn the Sefer Torah over. Regarding beginning to roll, meaning to wrap the cloth from the outside, he gives no reason. One might therefore have thought that he means only that it is permitted to begin rolling from the outside if one wishes, whereas fastening must specifically be on the inside. Magen Avraham therefore writes that this too is meant specifically, because of the concern that the Sefer Torah might, Heaven forbid, fall.

machatzit_hashekel.he: (ס"ק ו) כי אין כו' הוא היה זוכ' כו' מטעם דהמתחיל במצות א"ל גמור וא"כ אי לא היה יכול לקרות בתורה אלא הש"ץ א"כ הית' התפלה והקריאה בס"ת חדא מלתא והיינו אומרים כיון שהתחיל להתפלל יגמור המצות בהוצאת והכנס' ס"ת אבל כיון שלפעמים א' מתפלל וא' קורא וחזי' דתפלה וקריאה לא שייכים להדדי וכיון שסיים התפל' כבר עברה מצותו ואין לו שייכות להכנסת והוצאת ס"ת וכן הקורא עדיין לא התחיל במצות ג"כ אין לו שייכות להוצאת והכנסת ס"ת א"כ אפי' המתפלל קורא בתורה מ"מ אין לו זכיה בהוצאת והכנסת ס"ת דאין שייכות לו:
machatzit_hashekel.en: (s.k. 6) For there is no, etc. — he was entitled, etc., from the reason that one who begins a mitzvah is told to finish; and if so, if he could not read in the Torah except the prayer leader, then prayer and reading in the Torah would be one matter, and we would say: since he began to pray, he should finish the mitzvah with taking out and bringing in the Torah scroll. But since sometimes one prays and one reads, and we see that prayer and reading are not related to each other; and since when he finished prayer his mitzvah already passed and he has no connection to bringing in and taking out the Torah scroll — and likewise the reader, who has not yet begun the mitzvah, also has no connection to taking out and bringing in the Torah scroll; if so, even if the one praying reads in the Torah, nevertheless he has no acquisition in taking out and bringing in the Torah scroll, for he has no connection to it.

magen_avraham.he: בתוך התיק. פי' שאין מוציאו מהתיק וגוללו:
magen_avraham.en: Inside the case. Meaning, he does not remove it from the case, but rolls it while it remains inside.

mishnah_berurah.he: (כא) בתוך התיק - פי' שאין מוציאו מהתיק וגוללו מבפנים טועה שעי"ז נוח להקרע:
mishnah_berurah.en: (b) In the case, P. does not remove the hysteria from the inside, it is wrong that the congregation is comfortable to break:

turei_zahav.he: בתוך התיק טועה. דאם גולל בתוך התיק נוח להקרע:
turei_zahav.en: In the bag is wrong. Dham is running in the bag comfortable to break:

kaf_hachayyim.he: ו) וכתב עו"ש הרדב"ז דלכל הפירושים תורה שבע"פ מותר לאוחזן בין כשהוא ערום בין כשהם ערומים, והביאו כנה"ג שם. ועיין בא"ר שם שכתב דיש להחמיר אף בספרים שלנו כשידוע שידיו מטונפות. יעו"ש ולפ"ז גם בספרים דתורה שבע"פ יש להחמיר שלא לאוחזן כשידיו מטונפות:
kaf_hachayyim.en: 6) And the Radbaz wrote further there that according to all the explanations, the Oral Torah [sefarim] are permitted to hold, whether when he [the person] is bare or when they are bare; and the Knesses HaGedolah cited him there. And see the Eliyah Rabbah there, who wrote that one should be stringent even with our sefarim when it is known that his hands are soiled; see there. And according to this, also with sefarim of the Oral Torah one should be stringent not to hold them when his hands are soiled.

mechaber.he: אין המפטיר מתחיל עד שיגמרו לגלול הס"ת כדי שלא יהא הגולל טרוד ויוכל לשמוע ההפטרה:
mechaber.en: The Maftir may not start reading until they finish rolling the Torah so that the one rolling shouldn't be preoccupied and will be able to hear the Haftarah.

Although the Gemara and Shulchan Aruch mention only the Haftarah itself and not its blessings, he holds that this is the more logical reading, since the underlying reason governs the law. levushei_serad.en: <small>Magen Avraham, seif katan 11</small> “And that case of Yoma may be explained.” Meaning, in Yoma the blood of the goat was first passed upward because he carried the blood in his right hand, since that hand was already full. If he had first taken the blood of the bull, he would have needed to take it in his left hand, and it is burdensome to take something in the left hand when both hands are full. In Pesachim, however, he receives the full vessel first in his right hand and the empty vessel in his left. Our custom is therefore understood.

machatzit_hashekel.he:
(ס"ק ז) ויתחיל כו' דוקא קאמר כו' חוץ עב"י. ר"ל דבב"י הביא שני פירושי' אי הכוונה במ"ש ויתחיל מבחוץ הוא דוקא או ר"ל כלפי מ"ש שצריך להדק מבפנים עז"א ויתחיל אפי' מבחוץ וכיון דפשטות הל' משמע שדוקא יתחיל מבחוץ דומיא דמ"ש ויהדק מבפנים שהוא דוקא ולא מבחוץ וכמ"ש רמ"א הטעם ה"ה יתחיל מבחוץ ר"ל דוקא וא"א דס"ל להרב ב"י פי' זה עיקר דיתחיל פירושו שרשאי להתחיל אבל אם ירצה יתחיל מבפנים ה"ל להרב"י לפ' כן בש"ע כיון דבספרו ב"י מסתפק בזה הל' אי משמע דוקא א"ו דדעתו בש"ע באמת דדוקא יתחיל מבחוץ ואינו רשאי להתחיל מבפנים:
יש לחוש שתפול כו' בש"ע דמיירי שא' עושה הגבהה וגלילה ודאי די"ל שמא תפול כשיתחיל מבפנים משא"כ כשמתחיל מבחוץ דא"א שתפול לחוץ דהא מחזיקו במפה שמתחיל לגלול סביבו. ואף ע"ג שאח"כ כשיכרוך ויגיע המפה לצד פנים עדיין י"ל שמא תפול לחוץ ז"א כיון שכבר מוכרכת קצת במפה והוא מחזיק המפה בידו א"א שיפול לחוץ כ"כ מהר וכשיראה שהתחיל ליפול יחזיקנה בידיו אבל למנהגינו שא' מגביה והשני גולל ל"ל כ"ה שתפול אפשר מוד' מ"א דאם ירצ' יתחיל מבפנים כיון דבעל הגלילה עומד לפני הס"ת א"א שתפול מהרה ולא ירגיש:
machatzit_hashekel.en:
(s.k. 7) And he shall begin, etc. — he says specifically, etc., explicitly. Meaning: in Beit Yosef he brought two explanations — whether the intent in what he wrote "and he shall begin from outside" is specifically, or meaning relative to what he wrote that one must fasten from inside — that is, "and he shall begin" even from outside. And since the plain meaning of the law implies that he begins specifically from outside, similar to what he wrote "and he shall fasten from inside," which is specifically and not from outside — and as Rama wrote the reason: the same applies to "he shall begin from outside," meaning specifically. And it is impossible that the Rav Beit Yosef's explanation is the main one — that "he shall begin" means he is permitted to begin, but if he wishes he may begin from inside; Beit Yosef should have explained thus in Shulchan Aruch, since in his book Beit Yosef he is uncertain in this law whether it implies specifically, or whether his view in Shulchan Aruch is truly that he begins specifically from outside and is not permitted to begin from inside.
One must be concerned that it will fall, etc. — in Shulchan Aruch it speaks when one person does the raising and rolling; certainly one may say that perhaps it will fall when he begins from inside, unlike when he begins from outside, for it is impossible that it fall outward, for he holds it with the cloth with which he begins to roll around it. And even afterward, when he rolls and the cloth reaches the side of the inside, nevertheless one may say that perhaps it will fall outward — meaning, since it is already somewhat wrapped in the cloth and he holds the cloth in his hand, it cannot fall outward so quickly; and when he sees that it began to fall, he holds it in his hands. But per our custom, where one raises and the second rolls — there is no need for such concern that it will fall; for since the one rolling stands before the Torah scroll, it cannot fall quickly and he will not notice. It is possible that Magen Avraham agrees that if he wishes he may begin to roll it from the side of the inside, since the owner of the rolling stands before the Torah scroll.

kaf_hachayyim.he: ז) שם בהגה. ולא נהגו כן. פי' אף באותן שכתובין אשורית על העור ובדיו כגון מגילה כ"מ מפשטיות דברי רמ"א ז"ל וכ"כ א"ר או' א' והב"ד לעיל או' ה' וכ"כ בתשו' פנים מאירות ח"א סי' ע"ו, וכ"כ בביאור הגר"א, ודלא כמ"א סק"א. והטעם דלא נהגו כן אפשר לומר משום דהתוס' כתבו קצת משמע דל"ד ס"ת כמ"ש לעיל או' ה' והגמרא פ' חלק (סנהדרין דף ק' ע"א) ג"כ אפשר לפרש בענין אחר, ומ"מ כבר כתבנו לעיל או' ה' דיש פלוגתא בזה וע"כ נכון להחמיר לאחוז המגילה בעת הקריאה בבגד או בעמוד שלה או לפחות שלא יסיח דעתו מן הנטילה כמ"ש רמ"א ז"ל ודוקא לגבי שאר כתבי הקודש יש להקל בשלא יסיח דעתו מן הנטילה אבל לאח"ז ס"ת בלא מטפחת אין להקל בנטילה כמ"ש רמ"א ז"ל וכ"כ לעיל או' ג' יעו"ש:
kaf_hachayyim.en: 7) There, in the gloss: And they did not practice so. The explanation is that even with those that are written in Ashuris on leather and with ink, such as a Megillah, [they did not practice to be stringent], as is implied from the plain [reading] of the words of the Rama, of blessed memory; and so wrote the Eliyah Rabbah, ot 1, and we brought his words above in ot 5; and so it is written in the responsum Panim Me'iros, part 1, siman 76; and so it is written in the Biur HaGra; and not like the Magen Avraham, s.k. 1. And the reason that they did not practice so, one can say, is because the Tosafos wrote 'it is somewhat implied that it is not specifically a Sefer Torah,' as stated above in ot 5, and the Gemara in the chapter 'Chelek' (Sanhedrin, folio 100a) can also be explained in another way. And nonetheless, we have already written above in ot 5 that there is a dispute in this, and therefore it is proper to be stringent to hold the Megillah at the time of the reading with a garment or with its pillar, or at least not to divert his attention from the washing [of the hands], as the Rama, of blessed memory, wrote; and specifically regarding the other holy writings one may be lenient [with just] not diverting his attention from the washing, but for holding a Sefer Torah without a covering one should not be lenient [with just] washing, as the Rama, of blessed memory, wrote, and as [the author] wrote above in ot 3; see there.

chokhmat_shlomo.en: Seif 8. Regarding what Magen Avraham writes in seif katan 11, “and in Sotah 35 we say,” etc. Note: While studying this sugya, I found great difficulty with the Gemara’s question there: “But one may not perform mitzvos in bundles,” as we learned, “One may not give two sotahs to drink at once,” because one may not perform mitzvos in bundles. Why does the Gemara ask this? Let us say that the teaching there follows Rabbi Yehudah, and that this very point is the practical difference between the opinions. Rabbi Shimon explains that the reason is so that one woman should not become emboldened by the presence of the other. Accordingly, only there does this reason apply, while elsewhere, where this reason does not apply, one may perform mitzvos in bundles. Rabbi Yehudah says that this is not the reason, but rather because the verse states “her alone,” and not another with her, teaching that one may not perform mitzvos in bundles. We would therefore derive from that case to the entire Torah that mitzvos may not be performed in bundles, and the teaching that prohibits doing so would follow Rabbi Yehudah. This requires study. Examine it carefully.

They should not open the second. In Yerushalmi it says one should not take the second from the ark until the first is returned to its place; and so in Mateh Moshe chapter 11; and our custom is not thus — rather we take out both together and do not remove, etc. — end of his words; Darkei Moshe in the name of Rabbi Zechariah — and this requires further study: from where to act not like the Yerushalmi? And furthermore in our Gemara Yoma 56 it says: one descended before Rava and said he took the blood of the bull and placed the blood of the goat; and he said to him — say he placed the blood of the goat and took the blood of the bull — if so, behold you have that he must place the first before taking the second. And in Hagahot Maimoniyot he wrote one does not remove, etc., and brings proof from chapter 8 of Pesachim that we say "receive the full and return the empty," etc.; and he wrote that so is the Rosh chapter 2 of Shabbat in the name of Rabbeinu Yonah — and I searched in the Rosh and found nothing; and also I did not understand the proof — for we say in the Gemara "receive the full and return the empty" but not the reverse — for when one hands it to him immediately he must receive it; it supports Rashi who said one does not pass over mitzvot once it has come to his hand — end of his words; it implies specifically because he hands it to him he must receive — otherwise one need not receive; for if the reason is so he should not be idle — if so from where to support Rashi? And it is possible to say they are all one reason — therefore one does not pass over mitzvot so he should not be idle from mitzvot — and it is forced. And that of Yoma it is possible to say that if he took the blood of the bull he must take with the left, and therefore it is better to place the blood of the goat first so they take with the right; and that of Pesachim must be that the empty one holds in his left and the full he receives in his right — not so in Yoma where both are full; and this requires further study. One to whom they give to lift the Torah scroll and to roll — and he cannot do both — should lift and give to another to roll, for rolling is the main matter as written in siman 139; but when they honor him to hand him the mantles — rolling is preferable for it is the essence of the mitzvah, as we say: one who merited the incense says to his friend "you merited the coal pan with me" — see Yoma 70. When one sees a mitzvah he may leave it and go see another mitzvah, even though there is a mitzvah to see the performance of the mitzvah because "in the multitude of the people is the king's glory" — nevertheless he may pass from it (Rashi); and see Tosafot Yoma 33b — where we only do one mitzvah one is not obligated to do what came to his hand first — see there; and it is not necessarily so; and see Menachot 64b. And in Sotah 8 we say one does not give two sotot to drink together, and does not purify two metzora'im, and does not pierce two slaves, and does not behead two heifers together — for one does not do mitzvot in bundles, bundles; and Tosafot wrote it is forbidden to stand both in the azarah at once even though they do not drink together — and it is astonishing: would he forbid in such a case to stand two sacrifices together in the azarah and slaughter one and then the second, etc.? — see there. And the Gemara concludes with one kohen one does not give to drink, and with two kohanim one gives — and this requires further study on the Rambam who ruled plainly without distinguishing; therefore it appears to me that he explains the reverse — with one kohen he must give them one after another; therefore even if they stand at once in the azarah that is fine; but with two kohanim giving to drink at once — this one one and that one one — it is forbidden. And with this the difficulty of Tosafot who asked from two metzora'im is resolved — see there. And behold for the Rambam it is permitted to bring two infants at once and circumcise this one and then that one; but always at once with two mohalim is forbidden; and for Tosafot it is forbidden to bring them at once to circumcise them one after another, but to circumcise them at once with two mohalim is permitted; and if so with two Torah scrolls we practice like the Rambam that we are not particular about the bringing; and for Tosafot in wedding blessings one should not bring two cups before him at once but after Birkat HaMazon take one cup and bless seven blessings — so is Tur and Shulchan Aruch in Orach Chayim siman 62. And what Tosafot asked from two sacrifices — one may say specifically with two obligatory mitzvot it is bundles; and similarly with two obligatory korbanot it is forbidden to stand them together — so is Yoma chapter 5: we learned "they brought him the goat" — implying one does not bring bull and goat together — see there.
